title: RISO26 controlled facial tone master study — local paper/ink value instead of uniform face freckles
source_of_identity: Original authored Courier and Paper Artist in this repository; third-party sources are printing/technique comparisons only.
target: Physical AM/FM screen-dot area variation for the same original front-face source geometry in RisoPrint (two spot ink plates, paper, no RGB post effect)

observed.macro: Faces are distinguishable, but all facial planes are filled with visually equal-weight bright-red dots; there is no hierarchy across eye sockets, cheek surfaces and jaw turns.
observed.meso: The eyebrow/eye socket screen, the cheekbone screen and far jaw screen use the same apparent dot radius and concentration regardless of local reflected-light hierarchy. This creates a freckle-like polkadot look.
observed.micro: Screened dots have crisply separated Riso contact marks but are not independently adjusted per facial depth zone. Existing tiny eye, nose and lip engraving should remain solid ink.
observed.where: both front-view original people, across neutral, speech and smile frames
observed.root_cause: RisoCharacterInk paints every screened source part using the exact same RisoPaint.dots pattern (global screenDensity and dotCell), not different author-deposited master values.

references.title: Fish Guts Press close-up of blue/pink halftone eyes
references.rights: third-party print photo, technical visual study only (not copied/bundled)

observations.macro: Facial mark density varies: thin solid eye outline against broad hatching/dot-area fields; the pupil remains a distinct form.
observations.meso: Denser blue printed eye/temple value transitions into lighter pink/blue areas; paper still visibly separates cells.
observations.micro: Separate locally different circle/raster areas show tonal value rather than a universal surface of identical red dots.

references.translated_rule: Mid-density eye socket and light-density cheek/jaw on same physical spot master, preserving source eye contour and ink placement.

references.title: Tori Kudo — まなこ切る現実 (7-inch eye artwork)
references.rights: commercial record/visual owned by its artist and label; technique only
references.medium: Risograph-like eye printed artwork, exact press process not independently verified

observations.macro: Large continuous eye silhouette is framed by pale irregular background, not a uniform dot mask.
observations.meso: Dense ink builds the eye border while sparse dispersed specks remain secondary and not identity-bearing.
observations.micro: Local ink density varies with distance from dominant outline.

references.translated_rule: Keep source geometry and solid ocular lines; drop facial shadow-dot area for cheek fields, not by raster-blurring.

references.title: Original printed Angela Giarratana portrait, commercial artist print
references.rights: copyright holder/creator; observation only, no face/identity tracing

observations.macro: Readable eyes/nose/mouth preserved against mostly clean large cheek and forehead negative paper.
observations.meso: Shading density varies across forehead, face profile and under-chin rather than identical freckles over all planes.
observations.micro: Thin eye/nostril/ear shape contours remain sharp and independent from shaded masks.

references.translated_rule: Preserve previously reviewed eye/ear/lip geometry and reserved paper highlights; no fixed 30%-coverage speckles on all facial masses.

references.title: Hot Pink Press Risograph File Set Up Guide
references.rights: professional press educational guide, text paraphrase only

observations.macro: Each ink color is transferred through its own stencil/master, not arbitrary RGB output.
observations.meso: Independent grayscale plate artwork defines deposited stencil ink, including fractional tonal fields.
observations.micro: Different dot/halftone areas within one ink master are legitimate local gradations.

references.translated_rule: Three dot-size variants all use exactly the same chosen ink color, physical plate, registration angle, seed and cell.

features.topology: unchanged curved brows/orbits anchored to the original head, not a new phantom colored plane
features.edge: crisp same screen cells at smaller dot radius
features.negative: do not bleach/simplify iris, close paper eye, create ghosted duplicated print

features.topology: unchanged two original cheek wing/zygomatic contours and jaw transition
features.negative: keep original contour and nonuniform two cheek wings, not Gaussian blur or hard paint alpha

features.topology: contours remain curved around lateral jaw and below the head
features.edge: light 2-unit AM dot density, no detached red pebbles
features.negative: do not erase jaw line, lighten by alpha, fill whole face uniformly

mathematical_basis.screen_mode: AM: individual circle radius follows r = cell * sqrt(density/pi) (dotGain adjustment), FM: deterministic ranked sites at fixed radius. Both are real printed ink coverage, not CSS transparency.
mathematical_basis.registration: same per-plate transform and pattern angle for all tone levels
mathematical_basis.full_print_opacity: physical ink is opaque in path and uses original RisoPrint multiply blend of spot plates

required_artifact: before and after matched frames for both identities and both 16:9/9:16
one AM and one FM render
close-up facial field from named source part

independent_artistic_review.reason: Actual Chromium run 43746812507 AM and FM 16:9/9:16 side-by-side crops reviewed at native size. Original source outlines, eyes, ears and lip engraving remain intact; graded cheek/jaw dots shrink and form a clearer value hierarchy, with no evidence of alpha overlays or posterized silhouette loss. Still not source-identity or anatomy certified.

human_anatomy_fidelity.reason: no independently annotated identity-specific source landmarks, full profile or three-quarter source

permissions: No third-party reference images or file assets committed.
